nakedSingle.description: One empty cell has just one possible digit.
nakedSingle.concept: Candidates are the digits that can still fit in an empty cell.
nakedSingle.lookFor: Find a cell where the row, column and box rule out every digit but one.
nakedSingle.reasoning: Only one candidate remains, so that digit must go in this cell.
nakedSingle.example: The highlighted cell has one legal candidate. Notice what its peers exclude.
nakedSingle.tryIt: Choose that cell and place its remaining digit.

hiddenSingle.description: A digit has only one possible position in a row, column or box.
hiddenSingle.concept: Look at one digit across a unit, rather than all digits in one cell.
hiddenSingle.lookFor: Find the only empty position where that digit is still allowed.
hiddenSingle.reasoning: Other cells may have several candidates, but this digit has just one home in the unit.
hiddenSingle.example: The highlighted unit leaves one position for the target digit.
hiddenSingle.tryIt: Choose the unique position and place that digit.

nakedPair.description: Two cells in one unit have the same pair of candidates.
nakedPair.concept: A pair reserves its two digits for those two cells.
nakedPair.lookFor: Find two cells in the same row, column or box with exactly the same two candidates.
nakedPair.reasoning: Those digits cannot appear elsewhere in that unit, so eliminate them there.
nakedPair.example: The highlighted pair removes candidates from other cells in its unit.
nakedPair.tryIt: Mark every candidate the pair eliminates. No digit is placed yet.

pointingPair.description: Two candidate positions in a box align on one row or column.
pointingPair.concept: A box can confine a digit to one line.
pointingPair.lookFor: Find exactly two positions for a digit inside a box on the same row or column.
pointingPair.reasoning: The digit must stay in that box, so remove it elsewhere on the shared line.
pointingPair.example: Follow the highlighted line outside the box to see the eliminations.
pointingPair.tryIt: Mark every candidate removed outside the box.

hiddenPair.description: Two digits are hidden in the same two cells.
hiddenPair.concept: A hidden pair is found by following digits, not matching cell masks.
hiddenPair.lookFor: Find two digits that occur in exactly the same two cells of a unit.
hiddenPair.reasoning: Both digits belong to those cells; every other candidate there can go.
hiddenPair.example: The highlighted two cells contain the only positions for both digits.
hiddenPair.tryIt: Remove extra candidates from those two cells.

boxLineReduction.description: A row or column confines a digit to one box.
boxLineReduction.concept: A line can lock a digit inside a box.
boxLineReduction.lookFor: Find two or three positions for a digit in one line, all inside one box.
boxLineReduction.reasoning: The digit must appear in that box on the line, so remove it elsewhere in the box.
boxLineReduction.example: Follow the highlighted line into the box and find candidates outside it.
boxLineReduction.tryIt: Remove the digit from the other cells of that box.

nakedTriple.description: Three cells share only three candidate digits.
nakedTriple.concept: A triple reserves three digits for three cells in one unit.
nakedTriple.lookFor: Find three cells whose candidate union contains exactly three digits.
nakedTriple.reasoning: The three digits must fill those cells, even when their masks differ.
nakedTriple.example: The highlighted cells use different pairs but share exactly three digits.
nakedTriple.tryIt: Remove those digits from the other cells in the unit.

xWing.description: Two lines align the same digit in two crossing positions.
xWing.concept: An X-Wing links two rows or two columns by one candidate digit.
xWing.lookFor: Find two lines where a digit appears exactly twice in matching positions.
xWing.reasoning: The four intersections reserve this digit, so remove it elsewhere on the crossing lines.
xWing.example: Trace the four highlighted positions and the two crossing lines.
xWing.tryIt: Remove the digit outside the four pattern cells.

coach.identifyHiddenPair: Two digits can appear only in the same two cells. Remove their other candidates.

why.title: Explanation
why.givenTitle: This is a given digit of the puzzle
why.givenBody: It was on the board from the start, so there is no solving step to explain. Explanations are available for digits you place yourself.
why.unavailableBody: MICHI cannot prove this move with a supported technique in its pre-move state.
why.onlyCandidate: The row, column and box rule out the other digits. Only $digit fits here.
why.unitSearch: Look for a place for $digit in $unit.
why.solePosition: The crossed-out $digit marks show where it cannot go in $unit. This is the only place left.
